page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 is an x86_64 compute configuration based on the AMD EPYC 9J14 processor family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-per-vCPU ratio. The processor incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, accompanied by instruction support for AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES encryption.

The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without onboard local storage devices or GPU accelerators. Persistent data operations and operating system root disks necessitate the attachment of external network block storage volumes. Because storage performance depends entirely on remote volume provisioning, disk IOPS and throughput scale according to network-attached volume limits.

Benchmark evaluations reflect top-quartile results in single-threaded execution, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2067.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3058.98. Multi-core performance aligns with mid-tier benchmarks, recording 8087.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 14386.29 in PassMark CPU tests. While cached memory reads reach 603.65 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB memory read bandwidth falls into the lower quartile at 35.48 GB/sec. Synthetic LLM inference also reflects CPU constraints on medium models, generating 22.54 prompt tokens per second on 7B parameter architectures.

From a resource-density perspective, the machine provides high memory headroom per CPU core without requiring payment for superfluous compute threads. This configuration is effective for memory-bound workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute, such as Redis key-value stores, relational databases, text parsing pipelines, and mid-sized enterprise application services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Driven by dedicated 2.3 GHz AMD EPYC 9J14 processors across 4 physical cores with multithreading, it delivers an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The CPU architecture supports AVX-512 vector extensions and hardware-assisted encryption. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong text processing, whereas multi-core compute and uncached memory read bandwidth position within average or lower ranges. The instance provisions no integrated local disk storage and lacks hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block volumes for persistent data. Given its strong single-thread efficiency and substantial memory density relative to core count, this server profile is suitable for in-memory caching systems, relational databases, backend application servers, and mid-tier data processing.
